newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav copper mine to invest $80 mln by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav copper mine to invest $80 mln by 2000.

text.p: Yugoslav copper mine Rudnik bakra Majdanpek plans to invest $80 million by the year 2000 in its reconstruction, the Belgrade daily Politika reported on Thursday.
The Majdanpek mine is part of the Rudarsko-topionicarski basen Bor (RTB Bor) mining and smelting complex, which groups some 20 enterprises.

The Bor copper complex has invested $3 million in the reconstruction of the Majdanpek copper mine and will invest another $3 million by the end of the year, the paper quoted Majdanpek's acting manager Zivorad Stanisavljevic as saying.
Majdanpek mined a total of 11.78 million tonnes of material in January-May, up 3.28 million tonnes on the same period in 1996.
"The thirty percent January-May incease (on the same period last year) is encouraging and indicates the started mine reconstruction will give good results," Stanisavljevic said.
Results would have been better if recently purchased machinery had arrived on time, he added. Five new trucks were expected to arrive by the end of the year.

The mine expected to reach annual production of some eight million tonnes of copper ore soon, and after reconstruction expected to produce some ten million tonnes of ore annually, or between 30,000 and 35,000 tonnes of copper in concentrate.
Flotation technology has been improved and it can now process 23,000-24,000 tonnes of ore daily.

Geological exploration had determined reserves of two million tonnes of ore containing an average 0.5 percent of copper in the southern part of the surface mine. Additional drilling indicated 4.5 million tonnes of ore with the same copper content.
The ore currently exploited contains 0.3 and in some places 0.2 percent copper.
Exploitation of a 2.1-million-tonne deposit containing copper, zinc, gold and lead was expected to start by the end of next year.
"This is expected to be very profitable because of the rich metal content of the ore," Stanisavljevic said.
Experts from Majdanpek, Bor and specialised Belgrade institutes have been engaged to determine an adequate ore processing technology.
